summary: Evening 5xx floor after frontend accept-queue packing and runtime worker GPU swap
description: Customers (BrightDocs) reported a sustained elevated 5xx rate starting ~18:05 UTC during an evening traffic ramp. Errors were observed across streaming and short-text generation endpoints. Initial signs pointed to API gateway returning 502/503 and upstream runtimes showing worker restarts tied to GPU hot-swap events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In prod-us-east, send a mixed workload: 60% short generation requests (<=128 tokens) and 40% streaming sessions (server-sent-chunk style) for a sustained 10-minute window at 1.8x normal steady-state rate.
2) Confirm api-gateway accept queue depth increases and HTTP/2 streams backlog rises.
3) Observe runtime logs for NVML/driver warnings and worker runtime exits within 30-90s of the traffic spike.
logs: 18:06:12 api-gw-01 ERROR upstream 502 - accept_queue=512/1024 streams=240 backlog=78
18:06:17 runtime-worker-07 WARN NVML: GPU 0 reset detected; swapping worker process
18:06:19 runtime-worker-07 ERROR runtime: watchdog timeout, exiting (oom=false, gpu_reset=true)
investigation_notes: Observed correlation: accept-queue packing on api-gateway after recent idle-keepalive change (edge-proxy PR 1423) increased simultaneous stream multiplexing per connection.

Hypothesis A: Larger multiplexed streams increased head-of-line blocking leading to accept queue pressure and connection churn; this amplified NVML driver resets on noisy GPUs causing worker swaps and crash loops.

Hypothesis B: Autoscaler attempted to rehome pods during GPU driver short resets; during reattachment NVML errors triggered abrupt worker exits instead of graceful draining, causing momentary capacity loss and 5xx floor.
Checked autoscaler events: several scale-down/scale-up cycles between 18:04-18:09 for shard cluster shard-14.
Heap/proc checks: no user OOM seen; runtime exit traces reference GPU driver API errors and sudden device loss path.
Traffic pattern: mix of long-lived streaming sessions and high short-request fanout created atypical distribution of KV cache hot-shards (observed increased lock contention).

root_cause: Race between increased connection multiplexing (edge-proxy accept-queue packing) and transient GPU driver resets on a subset of nodes. The combination caused sudden worker process exits during device reinitialization, reducing usable capacity and producing elevated 5xx until throttling and rollback completed.
resolution: 1) Rolled back edge-proxy config change to previous accept/keepalive behavior in prod-us-east at 18:12 UTC. 2) Applied a temporary per-tenant streaming concurrency throttle for BrightDocs at 18:10 UTC. 3) Deployed runtime patch (nvml-graceful-recover) to canary to tolerate short NVML device lost and drain workers gracefully. 4) Adjusted autoscaler cool-down to avoid rapid rehome during transient GPU recoveries.
